The Governor summons and prorogues the State Legislature.

Important Rule:
• Gap between two sessions should not exceed six months.
The Governor summons and prorogues the State Legislature.

items: The maximum permissible gap between two sessions of the State Legislature is 6 months—a frequently asked question in polity prelims.
Remember that the power to summon and prorogue belongs to the Governor, whereas the power to adjourn a sitting belongs to the presiding officer (Speaker/Chairman).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Governor has the constitutional power to summon and prorogue sessions of the State Legislature.
There must not be a gap of more than six months between the last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.
Due to the six-month rule, the State Legislature must meet at least twice a year.
